A practice built for changing realities.

Legal questions rarely arrive in isolation. They sit inside families, workplaces, organisations, transactions and fast-changing technology.

Discuss your matter

Clear counsel across connected areas of life and business.

Susan Mute & Company Advocates is led by Susan Mute, an Advocate of the High Court of Kenya. The practice advises on personal, commercial, workplace, property and dispute matters, with a strong additional focus on data protection, privacy and ICT law.

That combination matters. A workplace issue may involve personal data. A new product may raise contract, intellectual-property and privacy questions at once. A family or property decision can require both sensitivity and careful documentation. The practice is organised to see those connections without losing sight of the immediate task.

Contemporary in outlook. Practical in delivery.

The aim is to make legal advice usable: to identify the real issue, explain the available routes and help clients understand what should happen next. Public legal education is a natural extension of that work, particularly where technology is changing how people and organisations exercise rights and manage risk.

Modern counsel for people, businesses and the digital economy.

The practice brings these areas together without treating technology law as separate from everyday life or commerce.

How the practice approaches a matter.

  • Begin with the facts, documents and the outcome the client is trying to achieve.
  • Explain the legal position in direct, understandable language.
  • Consider preventive, negotiated and formal options where each is available.
  • Keep confidentiality, data care and professional responsibility central to the engagement.
